newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria envisages $51 bln investment by 2000 - APS.
newsitem.headline: Algeria envisages $51 bln investment by 2000 - APS.

text.p: The Algerian government envisages investing 2,893 billion dinars ($51.7 billion) in the next five years, mainly in housing, agriculture, services and the oil and gas sectors, the official Algerian news agency APS said.

The five-year investment plan is part of a medium-term Social and Economic National Development Strategy drafted by a government think tank, the Social Economic National Council (CNES), which on Sunday wound up its 8th session to assess the country's economic situation.
The draft strategy document was handed to Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia at the end of the CNES meeting in Algiers, the official media said on Monday.
"The strategy centres on improvement of production in some sectors like agriculture, industry, hydrocarbons, irrigation and services," said APS summing up the document.
It envisages the government investing 289.3 billion dinars ($5.16 billion) in the housing sector, APS said.
Algerian officials say the country has a shortage of one million housing units for its 29 million people.

"We favourably welcome this national development strategy which will offer the managers an accurate picture of the challenges facing the country and the efforts needed to renew a lasting and sustainable development," Ouyahia said according to APS.

Algeria's economy, reversing eight years of stagnation in the wake of falling crude oil prices in the 1980s, grew around four percent in each of the past three years. The government forecasts five percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1997.
But the CNES report said growth was still shaky, with the economy relying on variable factors such as international oil prices and the climate.
Agriculture, growing at an average 20 percent in the past three years, and the services sectors were the main providers of jobs in the past two years.
Algeria had a record harvest of 4.6 million tonnes of cereals in the 1995/96 season, according to official figures.
The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas rose to $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from the year before, according to official data.
But the non-oil and gas industry, which provides jobs for more than 1.7 million people and produces about 20 percent of the nation's added value, is still struggling to adjust to the free economy.
Non energy industrial production fell seven percent in 1996 compared to the year before, said the National Office of Statistics in a report late in April.
